common_name: Riviera Bermudagrass (Cold-Hardy Seeded Common-Type Turf Cultivar)

planting.note: Broadcast hulled seed at 1-2 lbs per 1,000 square feet once soil is reliably above 65°F, then irrigate lightly several times a day until the stand fills in.

directions: Prepare a firm, weed-free seedbed and sow in late spring once soil temperatures hold above 65°F, keeping the surface consistently moist through germination. Riviera was developed at Oklahoma State University as one of the first seeded bermudagrasses bred specifically for improved winter survival, giving it noticeably better cold tolerance and earlier spring green-up than older common bermuda seed sources. Mow at 0.5-1.5 inches once established, and expect the same full-sun requirement, drought tolerance, and vigorous summer spread typical of common bermudagrass.
sources: Oklahoma State University Extension — Bermudagrass Variety Trials
Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Bermudagrass Varieties for Texas Lawns

common_name: NorthBridge Bermudagrass (Cold-Hardy Fine-Textured Hybrid Turf Cultivar)

planting.note: Install as sod, sprigs, or plugs from spring through midsummer, since NorthBridge is a sterile hybrid propagated only vegetatively.

directions: Lay sod or set sprigs into a full-sun site in warm weather and water frequently for the first two to three weeks to knit the stand together, then shift to deep, infrequent irrigation. NorthBridge is an NC State University hybrid release bred for a rare combination of traffic tolerance, rapid divot recovery, and cold hardiness, which has made it popular for sports fields as well as high-end lawns across the transition zone and Gulf South. It holds a fine, dense texture with regular mowing but, like other hybrid bermudagrasses, needs full sun and consistent fertility to stay competitive with weeds.
sources: North Carolina State University — Turffiles Bermudagrass Cultivar Reports
Sod Solutions — NorthBridge Bermudagrass Technical Notes

common_name: Tahoma 31 Bermudagrass (Drought- and Cold-Tolerant Hybrid Turf Cultivar)

planting.note: Install as sod or plugs from spring through midsummer, since Tahoma 31 is a sterile hybrid propagated only vegetatively.

directions: Install sod or plugs into a full-sun site during warm weather and irrigate frequently until the stand roots in, then taper to deep, infrequent watering. Tahoma 31 was released by Oklahoma State University in 2018 and stands out among hybrid bermudagrasses for pairing strong drought tolerance with winter hardiness well beyond the Gulf Coast's usual needs, plus a dark blue-green color that holds through the growing season. Keep it mowed low and on a regular fertility program to maintain its fine, dense texture, and expect quick recovery from wear once it is fully established.
sources: Oklahoma State University Extension — Turfgrass Variety Development
Sod Solutions — Tahoma 31 Bermudagrass Technical Notes
